facts.text: Lime Springs got its name from a lime‑rich spring that bubbled out of a limestone bluff near the site of the Lidtke Mill.
The original settlement, called Old Town, sat north of the current city along the Upper Iowa River and was platted in 1857.
When the railroad reached the area in the late 1860s, residents moved the town south of the river, platted as Lime Springs Station in 1867.
The historic Lidtke Mill, now a museum, stands on the riverbank and reflects the town’s early milling heritage.
Welsh ancestry is celebrated in Lime Springs, with local history and genealogy resources appealing to descendants of early settlers.
Lime Springs experiences cold, snowy winters with Arctic outbreaks and warm, humid summers influenced by Gulf of Mexico southerly flows.
